statement: A running model, not a calibrated one, and thinner than the wisteria model: there was no prototype of this plant to carry numbers over from. The sizes of its leaf, flower clusters and seed heads and its flowering months rest on published descriptions; how its free shoots bend rests on a bending test of a congener (Clematis flammula) and on a study of searcher shoots that includes another clematis; its leaf spacing, leaf width and how its leaflets hang were read from photographs; its rates (how far a shoot extends, how often it branches, how many nodes flower or set seed, the days within the published months) are assumptions of the right order, none measured on a plant; the weights by which a shoot chooses its route are copied from the wisteria model. Use its output to compare scenarios and to show what a design implies, not to predict dates, sizes or loads.

names.basis: One leaf form, one flower form and one fruit form, so none is named. The clusters stand out from the leaf axils on stiff stalks and face away from the stem (saucer-shaped flowers in axillary clusters, Cambridge University Botanic Garden; peduncle 0.4 to 8 cm and flower stalks 1.8 to 7 cm, Huang et al. 2024), and the seed heads stand on the same stalks.

phenology.budburstDoy.basis: New shoots are taken to start on 26 March, while the plant is in flower: the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh records flower trusses and new vegetative shoots of "a deep bronze red" together on 18 April (https://stories.rbge.org.uk/?p=8863). The day itself is from no source.

phenology.growthEndDoy.basis: Extension is taken to end in mid September. No dated source.

phenology.leafFlushDoy.basis: Follows the start of growth. On an evergreen only a leaf's first spring is an opening, and a leaf on new growth opens as that growth is made, so these days decide little.

phenology.autumnColourDoy.basis: Evergreen (RHS): the leaves do not colour in autumn, and the engine reads these days for deciduous leaves only. Present because every model carries every parameter.

phenology.leafFallDoy.basis: Evergreen (RHS): there is no autumn leaf fall, and the engine reads these days for deciduous leaves only. Old leaves in fact drop in summer (https://www.rainyside.com/plant_gallery/vines/Clematis_armandii.html); the model drops a leaf at the end of its last year instead (organs.leafLifespanYears).

phenology.floralInitiationDoy.basis: RHS pruning group 1: it flowers on shoots produced in the previous summer (https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/clematis/group-one-pruning-guide); Huang et al. 2024: the cymes come "from axillary buds of old branches". The flower buds are taken to be laid down in the leaf axils by the end of August; the days are from no source. The engine acts on the second day, and growth made after it forms buds as well.

phenology.flowerOpenDoy.basis: Inside the published flowering months: RHS "early to mid spring", which is March and April (https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/3923/clematis-armandi/details); Bean "produced in April" (https://www.treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/clematis/clematis-armandii/); March and April (https://plantdatabase.kpu.ca/Plant/clar, https://www.ashwoodnurseries.com/shop/clematis-armandii.html). The clusters of different nodes are taken to begin opening between 5 March and 2 April, so that with phenology.flowerLastsDays every flower is over by the end of April.

phenology.petalFallDoy.basis: Not read while phenology.flowerLastsDays is set: each node's clusters then last their own time from the day they open. Kept inside the same published months (10 to 30 April).

phenology.flowerLastsDays.basis: The flowers of a cluster open in succession, and the two clusters of a node are taken to be in flower for about three weeks between them. The whole display then lasts some eight weeks with its peak at the turn of March and April; the International Clematis Society has it in flower "for a month or more" (https://internationalclematissociety.org/?p=735). How long one cluster lasts is from no source.

extension.leaderMPerSeason.basis: No source gives a yearly figure. The plant is "vigorous" (RHS) and its growth rate rapid (https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/clematis-armandi/); "Stems to 6 m long" (Huang et al. 2024) and the plant its 4 to 8 m in 5 to 10 years (RHS). 2.5 m a season, less while it establishes, makes a main stem 6 m long in its third or fourth season. A size band is not a growth rate: an assumption of that order.

extension.lateralMPerSeasonByOrder.basis: Branches of the main stems, scaled down from the leader rate. Not measured.

extension.whipMPerSeason.basis: The pace of a long shoot of the year thrown by older wood: fast enough for it to make its planned length (organs.whipLengthM) in the season it starts. Not measured.

extension.establishmentFactorByYear.basis: Slower while it roots in: half pace in the planting year and most of it in the next. No source gives a figure.

architecture.trunkStemStartYears.basis: Two stems on the nursery cane and a third from the base in the second season. Nursery advice is to cut a new plant back so that it makes several stems, since an unpruned one makes long single stems (https://www.ashwoodnurseries.com/shop/clematis-armandii.html); the number is from no source.

architecture.nurseryCaneM.basis: A nursery plant in a two or three litre pot, tied to a short cane. Not measured.

architecture.maxBranchOrder.basis: Main stems, their branches and the branches of those follow the structure; anything finer is a shoot of the year. A limit of the model, not a count from a plant.

architecture.leaderLengthM.basis: A cap on the length of a main stem: "Stems to 6 m long" (Huang et al. 2024, https://zenodo.org/records/15001723); 4 to 8 m high (RHS); 4.5 to 9 m (https://internationalclematissociety.org/?p=735). A height band is not a route length, so this is an assumption taken from those figures.

architecture.lateralLengthMByOrder.basis: Caps on the length of a branch, scaled down from the main stem. Not measured.

architecture.lateralLengthSpread.basis: Branches are taken to vary by about a third either way. Not measured.

architecture.lateralChanceByParentOrder.basis: The chance that a stem branches where it passes a joint of the structure. High: every node carries a pair of axillary buds and the plant branches freely into a dense mass. Not counted on a plant.

architecture.budExtraDormancyChance.basis: Most buds of last year's wood are taken to break the next spring, a minority to wait. Not counted on a plant.

architecture.budExtraDormancyYears.basis: How long a bud that waits is taken to wait. Not counted on a plant.

architecture.maxStemsPerRoute.basis: Stems a few millimetres thick run several together along one lath or cable; a plant left untrimmed "can develop thatching that is hard to remove" (https://internationalclematissociety.org/?p=735). Three to a member is an assumption.

architecture.maxStemsPerPrimaryMember.basis: One more than on a lath or cable, a glulam member being stout enough to carry it. An assumption.

routing.occupancyCost.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better: a weight in the engine's choice of route, not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.downhillCostPerM.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better: a weight in the engine's choice of route, not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.uphillBonusPerM.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better: a weight in the engine's choice of route, not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.straightOnBonus.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better: a weight in the engine's choice of route, not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.riserBonus.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better: a weight in the engine's choice of route, not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.tierBonus.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better: a weight in the engine's choice of route, not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.roleDropChance.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better: a weight in the engine's choice of route, not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.noise.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better: a weight in the engine's choice of route, not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.giveUpCost.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better: a weight in the engine's choice of route, not a measurement or a description of this plant.

attachment.maxGraspDiameterMm.basis: No measurement exists for this plant. Extension advice for clematis in general: they "do best with thin supports", and "If the support is greater than 3/4 inch in diameter add twine" (University of Illinois Extension, https://extension.illinois.edu/sites/default/files/hkmw-_clematis.pdf); "the twining petioles cannot grasp thick materials" (University of Nebraska-Lincoln Extension, G1861). On this plant it is the stalks of the leaflets that coil, and they are 1/2 to 1 in. long (Bean), enough to go once round a support of about 6 mm; the main stalk, 3.6 to 11 cm (Huang et al. 2024), can hook round more. 12 mm is taken, between the two: a cable qualifies, a 40 mm lath does not, and on timber the plant has to be tied.

attachment.minPitchM.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model; not used: a leaf-stalk climber's stem lies along its support and does not coil round it.

attachment.pitchPerCircumference.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model; not used: a leaf-stalk climber's stem lies along its support and does not coil round it.

organs.leafSpacingM.basis: The length of stem between one pair of leaves and the next. No source read gives it. Read from photographs on Wikimedia Commons, against the leaflets in the same picture (5 to 16 cm, Huang et al. 2024): on the young shoots of Clematis armandii in the Ceanothus - Flickr - peganum.jpg and Ranunculales - Clematis armandii - 5.jpg the pairs stand somewhat less than a leaflet's length apart. To be measured on a plant.

organs.leafLengthM.basis: The reach of the whole leaf, from the stem to its farthest point along the way it points, as it is drawn: the main stalk stands out and bows over and the three leaflets hang nearly plumb from its end (photographs on Wikimedia Commons, see morphology.json leaf.leafletPosture), so the reach is about 0.62 of the parts laid end to end. The parts are published: leaf stalk 3.6 to 11 cm and leaflets 5 to 16 cm (Huang et al. 2024, https://zenodo.org/records/15001723); main stalk 1.5 to 4 in, secondary stalks 0.5 to 1 in, leaflets 3 to 6 in (Bean, https://www.treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/clematis/clematis-armandii/). This range draws leaflets about 8 to 13 cm long on main stalks of about 5.5 to 8.5 cm, the middle of what is published, the engine having one leaf size for a plant. The reach and the share are this project's, not a source's.

organs.leavesPerNode.basis: Leaves opposite (NC State Extension; the Kwantlen plant database has them compound and opposite).

organs.spurChance.basis: No spurs: this plant flowers from the leaf axils of last summer's shoots (Huang et al. 2024: cymes "from axillary buds of old branches"), not on short spurs.

organs.spurLengthM.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

organs.spurLeafCount.basis: No spurs are modelled for this plant.

organs.racemeLengthM.basis: What one flower record of this plant is: the two clusters that stand in the two leaf axils of one node, measured across both from the outermost flower of one to the outermost of the other. The parts are published: peduncle 0.4 to 8 cm, flower stalks 1.8 to 7 cm (Huang et al. 2024, https://zenodo.org/records/15001723), flowers 5 to 6 cm across (RHS). The span is this project's sum of them, not a source's.

organs.whipShareOfNodes.basis: The share of older nodes on the main stems and branches that throw a long shoot in a year: nearly all of them, up to the cap in organs.whipsPerYearMax. On the plant the year's shoots come mostly from last year's shoots; in this model they can come only from the stems that follow the structure, so those stems are made to throw as many as the whole plant would. Chosen so that a plant six to ten years old carries the dense mass of foliage the sources describe ("A large, vigorous evergreen climber", RHS; grown as a screen). Not counted on a plant.

organs.whipsPerYearMax.basis: A cap on the long shoots a plant throws in a year. With shoots of 0.6 to 1.8 m it gives an established plant some 200 m of new shoot a year and two to four thousand leaves, which clothes a frame of 6 square metres and what hangs from it. Chosen with organs.whipShareOfNodes; not counted on a plant.

organs.whipLengthM.basis: The length of a long shoot of the year where it finds nothing to hold: it arches out and hangs. No source gives the length of a year's shoot; of the order of the leader rate.

organs.leafLifespanYears.basis: Evergreen (RHS). A leaf is taken to live through the season it is made in and the winter after, and to fall in the summer of the next year (phenology.evergreenLeafFallDoy), as the new leaves come: "In summer the old leaves drop off the vine" (Rainyside Gardeners, https://www.rainyside.com/plant_gallery/vines/Clematis_armandii.html). So a leaf lives some fifteen months, and last year's leaves stand behind the flowers in spring. How long a leaf lives is from no measurement.

organs.clearStemHeightM.basis: The plant goes bare below: it will "leave its lower reaches bare after a few seasons" (https://internationalclematissociety.org/?p=735). No new shoots are thrown below this height; the height is from no source.

flowering.competenceYears.basis: Flowers on the shoots of its first summer in the ground: nursery plants are of flowering age, and young unpruned plants flower at the top of their stems (https://www.ashwoodnurseries.com/shop/clematis-armandii.html). An assumption.

flowering.maturityRamp.basis: A third of full strength in the first flowering spring, rising to full in the third. Not counted on a plant.

flowering.spurFloralChance.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.unprunedFactor.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.currentSeasonFlowersPerM.basis: Nodes in flower for each metre of last summer's shoot, each bearing its two clusters: about three nodes in four at full strength. The flowers come "usually paired along the stems" (https://internationalclematissociety.org/?p=735) and in "dense axillary clusters" (Bean), a mass of bloom (Cambridge University Botanic Garden); the share is from no source.

flowering.currentSeasonMinShootM.basis: A shoot shorter than this is taken not to flower. Not from a source.

pruning.summerLeavesKept.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

pruning.winterBudsKept.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

regrowth.shootsPerCut.basis: New shoots from a stem cut back hard. Sources disagree on how well it answers (RHS: it does not usually respond well to renovation; Clemson Extension: it regrows from the base); one or two shoots is an assumption.

thickening.tipRadiusSquaredMm2.basis: A young shoot taken as 4 mm thick (radius 2 mm). No measurement of this species was found. Its congener Clematis flammula, measured by Isnard, Rowe and Speck 2003, Annals of Botany 91:407-417 (read at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4241066/), has aerial climbing shoots of 10.2 mm2 in cross-section on average (about 3.6 mm across); the long shoots of C. armandi, which carry leaves of three leaflets up to 16 cm long, are taken as a little stouter.

thickening.radiusSquaredPerMetreMm2.basis: Chosen so that a long shoot of the year is 6 to 7 mm thick at its base and a main stem a little over a centimetre at ten years. That is the low end of what is published: the stems harvested as the drug Caulis Clematidis Armandii are "1-5 cm in diameter" (Hong Kong Chinese Materia Medica Standards, https://cmro.gov.hk/hkcmms/vol2/pdf_e/Caulis_Clematidis_Armandii_v2_e.pdf). The engine thickens a stem by the framework it carries and not by the long shoots of the year, which are most of this plant, so a larger number would thicken the young shoots too much before it thickened the old stems enough. How fast a stem thickens is from no source.

thickening.branchShare.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better: the share of a branch's thickness that the stem bearing it takes on. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

fruit.setShare.basis: The share of flowering nodes that go on to carry seed heads. That it fruits in gardens is published (clusters of plumed seeds, Oregon State University; feathery white fruit in early summer, https://plantdatabase.kpu.ca/Plant/clar; silvery seedheads, Ashridge Nurseries); how often is not, least of all for Britain. Two nodes in five is an assumption.

fruit.lengthM.basis: What one fruit record of this plant is: the seed heads of one node, measured across the cluster. Each head is a tuft of achenes 4 to 5 mm long with feathered tails 1.6 to 4.8 cm long (Huang et al. 2024, https://zenodo.org/records/15001723), so 4 to 10 cm across, and the heads stand on the stalks the flowers stood on, so the cluster is about as wide as the flowers were. The span is this project's sum, not a source's.

fruit.swellDays.basis: Days from petal fall for the styles to lengthen to their full 1.6 to 4.8 cm. From no source.

fruit.ripenDoy.basis: The tails fluff out and the achenes brown in June and the first half of July: fruit in June and July (https://plantdatabase.kpu.ca/Plant/clar); "fruiting from April to July" in the wild (Huang et al. 2024). The days within those months are this project's.

fruit.fallDoy.basis: The ripe achenes are taken to blow away between mid July and mid September. No source says how long the heads stay on the plant.

appendages.leafStalkCoilShare.basis: The share of leaf nodes, on a stretch the plant holds by itself, at which a leaf stalk has wound round the support. The stalks of its leaflets coil round a support that they touch and grip it (Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, https://stories.rbge.org.uk/?p=8863); how many do is from no source.

appendages.leafStalkLengthM.basis: Not the length of a stalk: the reach of the wound part, from the node to the far side of the turn it makes round the support. What winds is the stalk of a leaflet (Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh), which is "1/2 to 1 in. long and twisted" (Bean, https://www.treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/clematis/clematis-armandii/): enough for about one turn round a cable 4 or 5 mm thick, and that turn reaches the cable's thickness, the stalk's own and a little slack. The stem lies against its support, so the turn is drawn at the node.

appendages.prickleSpacingM.basis: Unarmed: no description of the plant mentions prickles or thorns.

appendages.prickleLengthM.basis: Unarmed: no description of the plant mentions prickles or thorns.

sideShoots.perMetrePerYear.basis: None: the flowers come straight from the axillary buds of last year's shoots, on stalks with bud scales at the base and no leaves (Huang et al. 2024: "Cymes 1- to many-flowered, from axillary buds of old branches").

mechanics.woodModulusMPa.basis: Structural bending modulus of a set shoot. Not measured on this species. Isnard, Rowe and Speck 2003, Annals of Botany 91:407-417 (read at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4241066/) measured the aerial trellis-forming shoots of its congener Clematis flammula var. maritima at 1.619 +/- 0.492 GN/m2; that figure is taken. It is about half the 3000 MN/m2 that Hattermann et al. 2022, Frontiers in Forests and Global Change 5:836247 (https://doi.org/10.3389/ffgc.2022.836247) found a searcher needs to span more than about 0.8 m, which agrees with a shoot that arches over and hangs where it finds no hold.

mechanics.greenShootModulusMPa.basis: The soft growing end of a shoot on the day it is laid down: a tenth of the set value (mechanics.woodModulusMPa), the proportion the generic values have. Not measured.

mechanics.woodSetDays.basis: Days over which a new stretch of shoot stiffens. Not measured. Young shoots of this plant stay soft and coloured (bronze-red, then green) for weeks (Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, https://stories.rbge.org.uk/?p=8863, records the new shoots still "a deep bronze red" in April); twice the generic month is taken.

mechanics.stemFreshDensityKgM3.basis: A fresh shoot is mostly water; 1000 kg/m3 as Chelakkot and Mahadevan 2017 (https://doi.org/10.1098/rsif.2017.0001) take for a young shoot. Not weighed.

mechanics.leafFreshMassPerAreaKgM2.basis: Worked out, not weighed, for the outline the engine takes for a leaf: a disc 0.56 of its length across, which for the mean leaf of this model (organs.leafLengthM, 0.12 m, a reach and not the leaf laid out) is some 37 cm2. The real leaf is three leathery leaflets (Huang et al. 2024, https://zenodo.org/records/15001723: "leathery"), each about 10 by 3.5 cm as drawn (morphology.json), some 80 cm2 of blade with its stalks; a leathery evergreen blade is taken at about 0.45 kg of fresh mass a square metre, so some 3.6 g a leaf, which is about 1 kg/m2 of the engine's smaller outline.

mechanics.inflorescenceFreshMassKg.basis: One flower record is one node: two clusters of eleven to eighteen flowers in all (morphology.json), each flower some 5 to 6 cm across of thin sepals on a slender stalk. Not weighed: about 0.3 g a flower is taken, 5 g a node.

mechanics.fruitFreshMassKg.basis: One fruit record is the seed heads of one node: three to five tufts of achenes 4 to 5 mm long with feathered tails (Huang et al. 2024). Not weighed: a couple of grams.

mechanics.searcherReachM.basis: The farthest a free shoot holds itself out before it stops lifting its end. Not measured on this species. Hattermann et al. 2022, Frontiers in Forests and Global Change 5:836247 (https://doi.org/10.3389/ffgc.2022.836247) put Clematis vitalba, a leaf-stalk climber of the same genus, among the tendril climbers, which with the root climber "spanned the shortest range of distances from 14 to 91 cm"; no figure is given for the clematis alone. 0.6 m is taken, inside that range, for a shoot carrying heavy evergreen leaves.

mechanics.leanDeg.basis: The least a free shoot leans from plumb where it sets out: the generic figure, an imperfection of the size engineers give a column so that its buckling can be computed, not a measurement of this plant. Given here only so that the plant's mechanics are its own set.

mechanics.leafWeightOffsetShare.basis: Where a leaf's weight hangs off the stem, as a share of its reach from the node (organs.leafLengthM). The leaflets, which are nearly all the weight, hang from the end of the main stalk (3.6 to 11 cm, Huang et al. 2024) and the reach is little more than that stalk with the leaflet stalks, so the weight sits near the far end of the reach. A choice, not a measurement.

tropism.turnPerM.basis: How sharply a growing free shoot turns towards the way it seeks, chosen not measured: about a right angle in two and a half metres of growth. Weak on purpose: the long shoots of this plant arch out and hang where they find no hold (photographs on Wikimedia Commons, Clematis armandii Badefols-sur-Dordogne.jpg, an arch hung with a curtain of shoots; Clematis armandii in the Ceanothus - Flickr - peganum.jpg, shoot tips nodding over) and do not stand up as a twiner's leader does.

tropism.lightShare.basis: How far the way a shoot seeks leans from plumb to the light. Chosen: a little past half way, as the plant climbs through shrubs and trees to the light (the Edinburgh plant "gained five metres in height through a Viburnum tinus", Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, https://stories.rbge.org.uk/?p=8863).

attachment.graspReachM.basis: How near a free shoot must come to a support for a leaf to take hold of it. What holds is the stalk of a leaf and of its leaflets (Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh: they coil round a support they touch), on a leaf reaching some 12 to 19 cm from the stem (organs.leafLengthM). 0.1 m is taken, short of the leaf's reach, since only the stalks wind. Not measured.

organs.leafTurnToOpenShare.basis: How far a leaf is turned from where its node sets it towards the open and the light. Read from photographs, not measured: the leaflets hang face out from the support whichever way the shoot runs, in a curtain (Wikimedia Commons: Clematis armandii Badefols-sur-Dordogne.jpg, Clematis armandii RJB.jpg, Ranunculales - Clematis armandii 3.jpg). More than the generic half.

phenology.evergreenLeafFallDoy.basis: The days in the year after its last season between which an old leaf falls: 9 June to 19 July. Rainyside Gardeners (https://www.rainyside.com/plant_gallery/vines/Clematis_armandii.html): "In summer the old leaves drop off the vine", and leaves blackened by winter wind "cling to the vine until summer". The days within the summer are this project's.
